newsitem.title: DUBAI: Egypt's foreign minister arrives in Riyadh.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's foreign minister arrives in Riyadh.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa arrived in Riyadh on Saturday for talks with Saudi officials on fighting in Sudan and said his country opposed the partitioning of Sudan.

"I do not think that it is possible for us to accept the partitioning of Sudan under any circumstances," Moussa told reporters at King Khaled International Airport where he was met by his Saudi counterpart Prince Saud al-Faisal.
During his two-day visit, Moussa would also discuss Arab affairs with Saudi officials.
Moussa said the fighting in Sudan was the result of internal developments in the country.

Sudan maintains that Ethiopia and Eritrea are behind clashes in the east and that both states are using rebels to fight for them. Egypt denies the presence of any foreign troops but other Arab states, like Jordan and Yemen, support Sudan's version of the events.
The Sudanese opposition in exile called on Thursday on Egypt, Sudan's powerful northern neighbour, to help overthrow the Khartoum Islamist government which took power in a military coup in 1989.

Egypt has not said it will help the rebels, despite its long dispute with the Sudanese government over the presence in Sudan of Egyptian Islamists fighting the Cairo government. Cairo has accused Khartoum of sheltering Moslem militants who tried to kill President Mubarak in Ethiopia in 1995.
Egyptian foreign ministry sources said Moussa would also deliver a letter to Saudi Arabia's King Fahd from Mubarak.
